# Running pandoc as a web server

If you rename (or symlink) the pandoc executable to
`pandoc-server`, or if you call pandoc with `server` as the first
argument, it will start up a web server with a JSON API. This
server exposes most of the conversion functionality of pandoc. For
full documentation, see the [pandoc-server] man page.

If you rename (or symlink) the pandoc executable to
`pandoc-server.cgi`, it will function as a CGI program
exposing the same API as `pandoc-server`.

`pandoc-server` is designed to be maximally secure; it uses
Haskell's type system to provide strong guarantees that no I/O
will be performed on the server during pandoc conversions.

[pandoc-server]: https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/blob/master/doc/pandoc-server.md

# Running pandoc as a Lua interpreter

Calling the pandoc executable under the name `pandoc-lua` or with
`lua` as the first argument will make it function as a standalone
Lua interpreter. The behavior is mostly identical to that of the
[standalone `lua` executable][lua standalone], version 5.4.
All `pandoc.*` packages, as well as the packages `re` and `lpeg`,
are available via global variables. Furthermore, the globals
`PANDOC_VERSION`, `PANDOC_STATE`, and `PANDOC_API_VERSION` are
set at startup. For full documentation, see the [pandoc-lua] man page.

[lua standalone]: https://www.lua.org/manual/5.4/manual.html#7
[pandoc-lua]: https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/blob/master/doc/pandoc-lua.md

# A note on security

1. Although pandoc itself will not create or modify any files other
   than those you explicitly ask it create (with the exception
   of temporary files used in producing PDFs), a filter or custom
   writer could in principle do anything on your file system. Please
   audit filters and custom writers very carefully before using them.

2. Several input formats (including LaTeX, Org, RST, and Typst)
   support `include` directives that allow the contents of a file to be
   included in the output. An untrusted attacker could use these
   to view the contents of files on the file system. (Using the
   `--sandbox` option can protect against this threat.)

3. Several output formats (including RTF, FB2, HTML with
   `--self-contained`, EPUB, Docx, and ODT) will embed encoded
   or raw images into the output file.  An untrusted attacker
   could exploit this to view the contents of non-image files on the
   file system.  (Using the `--sandbox` option can protect
   against this threat, but will also prevent including images in
   these formats.)

4. In reading HTML files, pandoc will attempt to include the
   contents of `iframe` elements by fetching content from the
   local file or URL specified by `src`. If untrusted HTML is
   processed on a server, this has the potential to reveal anything
   readable by the process running the server. Using the `-f html+raw_html`

import subprocess
def run(args,inp=b"",timeout=5):
    try:
        return subprocess.run(['./executable']+args,input=inp,capture_output=True,timeout=timeout)
    except Exception as e:
        print("timeout",args,e); return None
# Lua tests
for args,inp in [
 (["lua","-e","print(1+2)"],b""),
 (["lua","-e","print(_VERSION)"],b""),
 (["lua","-e","print(PANDOC_VERSION)"],b""),
 (["lua","-i"],b"print(42)\n"),
 (["lua","--"],b"print(1)\n"),
 (["lua","-e","foo("],b""),
]:
    r=run(args,inp)
    if r: print(args, r.returncode, repr(r.stdout[:500]), repr(r.stderr[:500]))

# server version?
for args in [["server","--version"],["server","-v"],["server","--unknown"]]:
    r=run(args)
    if r: print(args, r.returncode, repr(r.stdout[:500]), repr(r.stderr[:500]))

# argv0 behavior: symlink name?
import os, tempfile
os.makedirs("/tmp/pandoc_test",exist_ok=True)
for name in ["pandoc-lua","pandoc-server","pandoc-server.cgi","pandoc"]:
    p=f"/tmp/pandoc_test/{name}"
    try: os.unlink(p)
    except: pass
    os.symlink(os.path.abspath("./executable"),p)
    r=subprocess.run([p,"--version"],capture_output=True,timeout=3)
    print("symlink",name,r.returncode,repr(r.stdout[:400]),repr(r.stderr[:400]))
    r=subprocess.run([p,"-v"],capture_output=True,timeout=3)
    print("  -v",r.returncode,repr(r.stdout[:400]),repr(r.stderr[:400]))

messages.content: 0 `pandoc --list-output-formats` to print lists of supported formats. If the input or output format is not specified explicitly, pandoc will attempt to guess it from the extensions of the filenames. Thus, for example, pandoc -o hello.tex hello.txt will convert `hello.txt` from Markdown to LaTeX. If no output file is specified (so that output goes to *stdout*), or if the output file's extension is unknown, the output format will default to HTML. If no input file is specified (so that input comes from *stdin*), or if the input files' extensions are unknown, the input format will be assumed to be Markdown. ## Character encoding Pandoc uses the UTF-8 character encoding for both input and output. If your local character encoding is not UTF-8, you should pipe input and output through [`iconv`]: iconv -t utf-8 input.txt | pandoc | iconv -f utf-8 Note that in some output formats (such as HTML, LaTeX, ConTeXt, RTF, OPML, DocBook, and Texinfo), information about the character encoding is included in the document header, which will only be included if you use the `-s/--standalone` option. [`iconv`]: https://www.gnu.org/software/libiconv/ ## Creating a PDF To produce a PDF, specify an output file with a `.pdf` extension: pandoc test.txt -o test.pdf By default, pandoc will use LaTeX to create the PDF, which requires that a LaTeX engine be installed (see `--pdf-engine` below). Alternatively, pandoc can use ConTeXt, roff ms, or HTML as an intermediate format. To do this, specify an output file with a `.pdf` extension, as before, but add the `--pdf-engine` option or `-t context`, `-t html`, or `-t ms` to the command line. The tool used to generate the PDF from the intermediate format may be specified using `--pdf-engine`. You can control the PDF style using variables, depending on the intermediate format used: see [variables for LaTeX], [variables for ConTeXt], [variables for `wkhtmltopdf`], [variables for ms]. When HTML is used as an intermediate format, the output can be styled using `--css`. --- ## Specifying bibliographic data You can specify an external bibliography using the `bibliography` metadata field in a YAML metadata section or the `--bibliography` command line argument. If you want to use multiple bibliography files, you can supply multiple `--bibliography` arguments or set `bibliography` metadata field to YAML array. A bibliography may have any of these formats: Format File extension ------------ -------------- BibLaTeX .bib BibTeX .bibtex CSL JSON .json CSL YAML .yaml RIS .ris Note that `.bib` can be used with both BibTeX and BibLaTeX files; use the extension `.bibtex` to force interpretation as BibTeX. In BibTeX and BibLaTeX databases, pandoc parses LaTeX markup inside fields such as `title`; in CSL YAML databases, pandoc Markdown; and in CSL JSON databases, an [HTML-like markup][CSL markup specs]: `...` : italics `...` : bold

A custom reader is a Lua script that defines one function,
Reader, which takes a string as input and returns a Pandoc
AST.  See the [Lua filters documentation] for documentation
of the functions that are available for creating pandoc
AST elements.  For parsing, the [lpeg] parsing library
is available by default. To see a sample custom reader:

If you want your custom reader to have access to reader options
(e.g. the tab stop setting), you give your Reader function a
second `options` parameter.

A custom writer is a Lua script that defines a function
that specifies how to render each element in a Pandoc AST.
See the [djot-writer.lua] for a full-featured example.

Note that custom writers have no default template.  If you want
to use `--standalone` with a custom writer, you will need to
specify a template manually using `--template` or add a new
default template with the name
`default.NAME_OF_CUSTOM_WRITER.lua` to the `templates`
subdirectory of your user data directory (see [Templates]).

# Reproducible builds

Some of the document formats pandoc targets (such as EPUB,
docx, and ODT) include build timestamps in the generated document.
That means that the files generated on successive builds will
differ, even if the source does not.  To avoid this, set the
`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` environment variable, and the timestamp will
be taken from it instead of the current time.
`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` should contain an integer unix timestamp
(specifying the number of seconds since midnight UTC January 1, 1970).

import copy, re, unicodedata

def B(t, c=None):
    if c is None:
        # caller determines; for no-arg constructors pass explicit special? We'll return without c only if t in nullary set and c is None marker via B0
        return {"t": t, "c": []}
    return {"t": t, "c": c}
def B0(t):
    return {"t": t}
def I(t, c=None):
    if c is None:
        return {"t": t}
    return {"t": t, "c": c}
def Attr(ident="", classes=None, kvs=None):
    return [ident, list(classes or []), [[k,v] for k,v in (kvs or [])]]
def empty_attr():
    return ["", [], []]
def is_block(x):
    return isinstance(x, dict) and "t" in x

# stringify inlines/blocks to plain text like pandoc's stringify
def stringify(x):
    if x is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(x, str):
        return x
    if isinstance(x, list):
        return "".join(stringify(i) for i in x)
    if isinstance(x, dict):
        t = x.get("t"); c = x.get("c")
        if t == "Str":
            return c
        if t == "Space":
            return " "
        if t == "SoftBreak":
            return " "
        if t == "LineBreak":
            return "\n"
        if t == "Code":
            return c[1]
        if t == "Math":
            return c[1]
        if t == "RawInline":
            return ""  # pandoc stringify ignores raw? check later maybe returns?
        if t == "Quoted":
            return stringify(c[1])
        if t in ("Emph","Strong","Underline","Strikeout","Superscript","Subscript","SmallCaps","Span"):
            # span c is [attr,inlines]
            if t=="Span": return stringify(c[1])
            return stringify(c)
        if t in ("Link","Image"):
            return stringify(c[1])
        if t == "Cite":
            return stringify(c[1])
        if t == "Note":
            return ""
        # blocks
        if t in ("Para","Plain"):
            return stringify(c) + "\n"
        if t == "Header":
            return stringify(c[2]) + "\n"
        if t == "CodeBlock":
            return c[1] + "\n"
        if t == "RawBlock":
            return c[1] + "\n"
        if t == "LineBlock":
            return "\n".join(stringify(line) for line in c) + "\n"
        if t in ("BlockQuote","Div","Figure"):
            if t=="Div": return stringify(c[1])
            if t=="Figure": return stringify(c[2]) if len(c)>2 else stringify(c[1])
            return stringify(c)
        if t in ("BulletList",):
            return "".join(stringify(item) for item in c)
        if t == "OrderedList":
            return "".join(stringify(item) for item in c[1])
        if t == "DefinitionList":
            s=""
            for term, defs in c:
                s+=stringify(term)+"\n"
                for d in defs: s+=stringify(d)
            return s
        if t == "Table":
            # stringify cells roughly
            return ""
        if t == "HorizontalRule":
            return "\n"
        # meta
        if t in ("MetaInlines","MetaBlocks","MetaList"):
            return stringify(c)
        if t == "MetaString":
            return c
        if t == "MetaBool":
            return "true" if c else "false"
        if t == "MetaMap":
            return "".join(stringify(v) for v in c.values()) if isinstance(c, dict) else ""
        return stringify(c) if c is not None else ""
    return str(x)

def stringify_trim(x):
    s = stringify(x)
    # pandoc stringify for headers etc ? trim spaces
    return s.strip()

def ascii_transliterate(s):
    # NFKD, drop non-ascii and combining
    out=""
    for ch in s:
        decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ch)
        for d in decomposed:
            if ord(d) < 128 and not unicodedata.combining(d):
                out += d
            elif unicodedata.combining(d):
                continue
            else:
                # drop
                pass
    return out

def auto_identifier(inlines, exts, used, fallback_section=True):
    text = stringify(inlines)
    # stringify for header may have newline removal etc
    text = text.strip("\n")
    gfm = exts.get("gfm_auto_identifiers", False) if exts else False
    ascii_only = exts.get("ascii_identifiers", False) if exts else False
    if ascii_only:
        text = ascii_transliterate(text)
    text = text.lower()
    if gfm:
        # keep letters/numbers/_/-, spaces -> -
        out=""
        for ch in text:
            if ch == " " or ch == "\t" or ch == "\n":
                out += "-"
            elif ch == "_" or ch == "-" or ch.isalnum():
                # isalnum includes unicode letters
                out += ch
            else:
                pass
        # gfm in commonmark reader: spaces? collapse? observed a  b (in ast single Space) -> single -
        ident = out
        # In pandoc markdown reader with gfm_auto_identifiers, empty -> section (fallback). In commonmark reader, no fallback - caller controls fallback_section
        if not ident and fallback_section:
            ident = "section"
    else:
        # pandoc: keep alnum _ - . and spaces; split words join -
        filtered_chars=[]
        for ch in text:
            if ch.isalnum() or ch in "_-.":
                filtered_chars.append(ch)
            elif ch in " \t\n\r\f\v":
                filtered_chars.append(" ")
            else:
                pass
        filtered="".join(filtered_chars)
        words = filtered.split()
        ident = "-".join(words)
        # drop leading until first letter
        i=0
        while i < len(ident) and not ident[i].isalpha():
            i+=1
        ident = ident[i:]
        if not ident and fallback_section:
            ident = "section"
    # dedup
    base = ident
    if used is not None:
        if ident not in used:
            used.add(ident)
            return ident
        # pandoc suffix -1, -2 ... find first unused starting 1
        n=1

                if i<len(text) and text[i]==':': i+=1
                val,i=self._parse_flow(text,i)
                result[str(key)]=val
                while i<len(text) and text[i] in ' \t\n': i+=1
                if i<len(text) and text[i]==',': i+=1
                elif i<len(text) and text[i]=='}': i+=1; break

# Defaults files

The `--defaults` option may be used to specify a package
of options, in the form of a YAML or JSON file. Examples in
this section will be given in YAML, but the equivalent forms in
JSON will also work.

Fields that are omitted will just have their regular
default values.  So a defaults file can be as simple as
one line:

``` yaml
verbosity: INFO
```

or in JSON:

``` json
{ "verbosity": "INFO" }
```

In fields that expect a file path (or list of file paths), the
following syntax may be used to interpolate environment variables:

``` yaml
csl:  ${HOME}/mycsldir/special.csl
```

`${USERDATA}` may also be used; this will always resolve to the
user data directory that is current when the defaults file is
parsed, regardless of the setting of the environment
variable `USERDATA`.

`${.}` will resolve to the directory containing the defaults
file itself.  This allows you to refer to resources contained
in that directory:

``` yaml
epub-cover-image: ${.}/cover.jpg
epub-metadata: ${.}/meta.xml
resource-path:
- .             # the working directory from which pandoc is run
- ${.}/images   # the images subdirectory of the directory
                # containing this defaults file
```

This environment variable interpolation syntax *only* works in
fields that expect file paths.

Defaults files can be placed in the `defaults` subdirectory of
the user data directory and used from any directory.  For
example, one could create a file specifying defaults for writing
letters, save it as `letter.yaml` in the `defaults` subdirectory
of the user data directory, and then invoke these defaults
from any directory using `pandoc --defaults letter`
or `pandoc -dletter`.

When multiple defaults are used, their contents will be combined.

Note that, where command-line arguments may be repeated
(`--metadata-file`, `--css`, `--include-in-header`,
`--include-before-body`, `--include-after-body`, `--variable`,
`--metadata`, `--syntax-definition`), the values specified on
the command line will combine with values specified in the
defaults file, rather than replacing them.

The following tables show the mapping between the command line and
defaults file entries.

+----------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| command line                     | defaults file                     |
+:=================================+:==================================+
| ```                              | ``` yaml                          |
| foo.md                           | input-file: foo.md                |
| ```                              | ```                               |
+----------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| ```                              | ``` yaml                          |
| foo.md bar.md                    | input-files:                      |
|                                  |   - foo.md                        |
|                                  |   - bar.md                        |
| ```                              | ```                               |
+----------------------------------+-----------------------------------+

The value of `input-files` may be left empty to indicate input from
stdin, and it can be an empty sequence `[]` for no input.

## General options

+----------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| command line                     | defaults file                     |

# This script enables bash autocompletion for pandoc.  To enable
# bash completion, add this to your .bashrc:
# eval "$(pandoc --bash-completion)"

_pandoc()
{
    local cur prev opts lastc informats outformats highlight_styles datafiles
    COMPREPLY=()
    cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"
    prev="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD-1]}"

    # These should be filled in by pandoc:
    opts="%s"
    informats="%s"
    outformats="%s"
    highlight_styles="%s"
    datafiles="%s"

    case "${prev}" in
         --from|-f|--read|-r)
             COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${informats}" -- ${cur}) )
             return 0
             ;;
         --to|-t|--write|-w|-D|--print-default-template)
             COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${outformats}" -- ${cur}) )
             return 0
             ;;
         --email-obfuscation)
             COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "references javascript none" -- ${cur}) )
             return 0
             ;;
         --ipynb-output)
             COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "all none best" -- ${cur}) )
             return 0
             ;;
         --pdf-engine)
             COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "pdflatex lualatex xelatex latexmk tectonic wkhtmltopdf weasyprint prince context pdfroff groff" -- ${cur}) )
             return 0
             ;;
         --print-default-data-file)
             COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${datafiles}" -- ${cur}) )
             return 0
             ;;
         --wrap)
             COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "auto none preserve" -- ${cur}) )
             return 0
             ;;
         --track-changes)
             COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "accept reject all" -- ${cur}) )
             return 0
             ;;
         --reference-location)
             COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "block section document" -- ${cur}) )
             return 0
             ;;
         --top-level-division)
             COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "section chapter part" -- ${cur}) )
             return 0
             ;;
         --highlight-style|--print-highlight-style)
             COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${highlight_styles}" -- ${cur}) )
             return 0
             ;;
         --eol)
             COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "crlf lf native" -- ${cur}) )
             return 0
             ;;
         --markdown-headings)
             COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "setext atx" -- ${cur}) )
             return 0
             ;;
         *)
             ;;
    esac

    case "${cur}" in
         -*)
             COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${opts}" -- ${cur}) )
             return 0
             ;;
         *)
             local IFS=$'\n'
             COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -X '' -f "${cur}") )
             return 0
             ;;
    esac

}

python3 << 'PY'
import re, json
lines=open("/tmp/help.txt").read().splitlines()[1:]
descs=[]
for line in lines:
    if not line.strip(): continue
    short_str=line[2:22].strip() if len(line)>=22 else line.strip()
    long_str=line[24:].strip() if len(line)>24 else ""
    shorts=[]
    if short_str:
        # split by ", " but placeholder no comma
        for part in short_str.split(", "):
            # -x or -x placeholder or -x[placeholder]
            ch=part[1]
            rest=part[2:]
            shorts.append([ch, rest])
    longs=[]
    if long_str:
        # split carefully: ", --"
        parts=re.split(r', (?=--)', long_str)
        for part in parts:
            # --name followed by =placeholder or [=placeholder] or nothing
            m=re.match(r'--([A-Za-z0-9\-]+)(.*)',part)
            name=m.group(1); rest=m.group(2)
            longs.append([name,rest])
    # kind
    kind="no"
    placeholder=""
    if longs:
        r=longs[0][1]
        if r.startswith("[="):
            kind="opt"; placeholder=r[2:-1]
        elif r.startswith("="):
            kind="req"; placeholder=r[1:]
    descs.append({"short_str":short_str,"long_str":long_str,"shorts":shorts,"longs":longs,"kind":kind,"placeholder":placeholder})
print(len(descs))
for d in descs[:20]: print(d)
open("/tmp/descs.json","w").write(json.dumps(descs,indent=1))

### Extension: `yaml_metadata_block` ###

A [YAML] metadata block is a valid YAML object, delimited by a line of three
hyphens (`---`) at the top and a line of three hyphens (`---`) or three dots
(`...`) at the bottom.  The initial line `---` must not be followed by a blank
line. A YAML metadata block may occur anywhere in the document, but if
it is not at the beginning, it must be preceded by a blank line.
(Note that JSON may be used as well, because JSON is a subset of YAML.)

Note that, because of the way pandoc concatenates input files
when several are provided, you may also keep the metadata in a
separate YAML file and pass it to pandoc as an argument, along
with your Markdown files:

    pandoc chap1.md chap2.md chap3.md metadata.yaml -s -o book.html

Just be sure that the YAML file begins with `---` and ends with `---` or
`...`. Alternatively, you can use the `--metadata-file` option. Using
that approach however, you cannot reference content (like footnotes)
from the main Markdown input document.

Metadata will be taken from the fields of the YAML object and added to any
existing document metadata.  Metadata can contain lists and objects (nested
arbitrarily), but all string scalars will be interpreted as Markdown.  Fields
with names ending in an underscore will be ignored by pandoc.  (They may be
given a role by external processors.)  Field names must not be
interpretable as YAML numbers or boolean values (so, for
example, `yes`, `True`, and `15` cannot be used as field names).

A document may contain multiple metadata blocks.  If two
metadata blocks attempt to set the same field, the value from
the second block will be taken.

Each metadata block is handled internally as an independent YAML document.
This means, for example, that any YAML anchors defined in a block cannot be
referenced in another block.

When pandoc is used with `-t markdown` to create a Markdown document,
a YAML metadata block will be produced only if the `-s/--standalone`
option is used.  All of the metadata will appear in a single block
at the beginning of the document.

Note that [YAML] escaping rules must be followed. Thus, for example,
if a title contains a colon, it must be quoted, and if it contains a
backslash escape, then it must be ensured that it is not treated as a
[YAML escape sequence]. The pipe character (`|`) can be used to begin
an indented block that will be interpreted literally, without need for
escaping. This form is necessary when the field contains blank lines
or block-level formatting:

    ---
    title:  'This is the title: it contains a colon'
    author:
    - Author One

### Extension: `pandoc_title_block` ###

If the file begins with a title block

    % title
    % author(s) (separated by semicolons)
    % date

it will be parsed as bibliographic information, not regular text.  (It
will be used, for example, in the title of standalone LaTeX or HTML
output.)  The block may contain just a title, a date and an author,
or all three elements. If you want to include an author but no
title, or a title and a date but no author, you need a blank line:

```
%
% Author
```

```
% My title
%
% June 15, 2006
```

The title may occupy multiple lines, but continuation lines must
begin with leading space, thus:

```
% My title
```

Four kinds of tables may be used. The first three kinds presuppose the use of
a fixed-width font, such as Courier. The fourth kind can be used with
proportionally spaced fonts, as it does not require lining up columns.

### Extension: `table_captions` ###

A caption may optionally be provided with all 4 kinds of tables (as
illustrated in the examples below). A caption is a paragraph beginning
with the string `Table:` (or `table:` or just `:`), which will be stripped
off. It may appear either before or after the table.

### Extension: `simple_tables` ###

Simple tables look like this:

      Right     Left     Center     Default
    -------     ------ ----------   -------
         12     12        12            12
        123     123       123          123
          1     1          1             1

    Table:  Demonstration of simple table syntax.

The header and table rows must each fit on one line.  Column
alignments are determined by the position of the header text relative
to the dashed line below it:[^4]

  - If the dashed line is flush with the header text on the right side
    but extends beyond it on the left, the column is right-aligned.
  - If the dashed line is flush with the header text on the left side
    but extends beyond it on the right, the column is left-aligned.
  - If the dashed line extends beyond the header text on both sides,
    the column is centered.
  - If the dashed line is flush with the header text on both sides,
    the default alignment is used (in most cases, this will be left).

[^4]:  This scheme is due to Michel Fortin, who proposed it on the
       [Markdown discussion list](http://six.pairlist.net/pipermail/markdown-discuss/2005-March/001097.html).

The table must end with a blank line, or a line of dashes followed by
a blank line.

The column header row may be omitted, provided a dashed line is used
to end the table. For example:

    -------     ------ ----------   -------
         12     12        12             12
        123     123       123           123
          1     1          1              1
    -------     ------ ----------   -------

When the header row is omitted, column alignments are determined on the basis
of the first line of the table body. So, in the tables above, the columns
would be right, left, center, and right aligned, respectively.

### Extension: `multiline_tables` ###

Multiline tables allow header and table rows to span multiple lines
of text (but cells that span multiple columns or rows of the table are
not supported).  Here is an example:

    -------------------------------------------------------------
     Centered   Default           Right Left
      Header    Aligned         Aligned Aligned
    ----------- ------- --------------- -------------------------
       First    row                12.0 Example of a row that
                                        spans multiple lines.

      Second    row                 5.0 Here's another one. Note
                                        the blank line between
                                        rows.
    -------------------------------------------------------------

    Table: Here's the caption. It, too, may span
    multiple lines.

These work like simple tables, but with the following differences:

  - They must begin with a row of dashes, before the header text
    (unless the header row is omitted).
  - They must end with a row of dashes, then a blank line.
  - The rows must be separated by blank lines.

In multiline tables, the table parser pays attention to the widths of
the columns, and the writers try to reproduce these relative widths in
the output. So, if you find that one of the columns is too narrow in the
output, try widening it in the Markdown source.

The header may be omitted in multiline tables as well as simple tables:

    ----------- ------- --------------- -------------------------
       First    row                12.0 Example of a row that
                                        spans multiple lines.

      Second    row                 5.0 Here's another one. Note
                                        the blank line between
                                        rows.
    ----------- ------- --------------- -------------------------

    : Here's a multiline table without a header.

It is possible for a multiline table to have just one row, but the row
should be followed by a blank line (and then the row of dashes that ends
the table), or the table may be interpreted as a simple table.

### Extension: `grid_tables` ###

Grid tables look like this:

    : Sample grid table.

    +---------------+---------------+--------------------+
    | Fruit         | Price         | Advantages         |
    +===============+===============+====================+
    | Bananas       | $1.34         | - built-in wrapper |
    |               |               | - bright color     |
    +---------------+---------------+--------------------+
    | Oranges       | $2.10         | - cures scurvy     |
    |               |               | - tasty            |
    +---------------+---------------+--------------------+

The row of `=`s separates the header from the table body,
and can be omitted for a headerless table. The cells of grid
tables may contain arbitrary block elements (multiple
paragraphs, code blocks, lists, etc.).

Cells can span multiple columns or rows:

    +---------------------+----------+
    | Property            | Earth    |
    +=============+=======+==========+
    |             | min   | -89.2 °C |
    | Temperature +-------+----------+
    | 1961-1990   | mean  | 14 °C    |
    |             +-------+----------+
    |             | max   | 56.7 °C  |
    +-------------+-------+----------+

A table header may contain more than one row:

    +---------------------+-----------------------+
    | Location            | Temperature 1961-1990 |
    |                     | in degree Celsius     |
    |                     +-------+-------+-------+
    |                     | min   | mean  | max   |
    +=====================+=======+=======+=======+
    | Antarctica          | -89.2 | N/A   | 19.8  |
    +---------------------+-------+-------+-------+
    | Earth               | -89.2 | 14    | 56.7  |
    +---------------------+-------+-------+-------+

Alignments can be specified as with pipe tables, by putting
colons at the boundaries of the separator line after the
header:

    +---------------+---------------+--------------------+
    | Right         | Left          | Centered           |
    +==============:+:==============+:==================:+
    | Bananas       | $1.34         | built-in wrapper   |
    +---------------+---------------+--------------------+

For headerless tables, the colons go on the top line instead:

    +--------------:+:--------------+:------------------:+
    | Right         | Left          | Centered           |
    +---------------+---------------+--------------------+

A table foot can be defined by enclosing it with separator lines
that use `=` instead of `-`:

     +---------------+---------------+
     | Fruit         | Price         |
     +===============+===============+
     | Bananas       | $1.34         |
     +---------------+---------------+
     | Oranges       | $2.10         |
     +===============+===============+
     | Sum           | $3.44         |
     +===============+===============+

The foot must always be placed at the very bottom of the table.

Grid tables can be created easily using Emacs' table-mode
(`M-x table-insert`).

### Extension: `pipe_tables` ###

Pipe tables look like this:

    | Right | Left | Default | Center |
    |------:|:-----|---------|:------:|
    |   12  |  12  |    12   |    12  |
    |  123  |  123 |   123   |   123  |
    |    1  |    1 |     1   |     1  |

      : Demonstration of pipe table syntax.

The syntax is identical to [PHP Markdown Extra tables].  The beginning and
ending pipe characters are optional, but pipes are required between all
columns.  The colons indicate column alignment as shown.  The header
cannot be omitted.  To simulate a headerless table, include a header
with blank cells.

Since the pipes indicate column boundaries, columns need not be vertically
aligned, as they are in the above example.  So, this is a perfectly
legal (though ugly) pipe table:

    fruit| price
    -----|-----:
    apple|2.05
    pear|1.37
    orange|3.09

The cells of pipe tables cannot contain block elements like paragraphs
and lists, and cannot span multiple lines.  If any line of the
Markdown source is longer than the column width (see `--columns`),
then the table will take up the full text width and the cell
contents will wrap, with the relative cell widths determined by
the number of dashes in the line separating the table header
from the table body. (For example `---|-` would make the first column 3/4
and the second column 1/4 of the full text width.)
On the other hand, if no lines are wider than column width, then
cell contents will not be wrapped, and the cells will be sized
to their contents.

Note:  pandoc also recognizes pipe tables of the following
form, as can be produced by Emacs' orgtbl-mode:

    | One | Two   |
    |-----+-------|
    | my  | table |
    | is  | nice  |

The difference is that `+` is used instead of `|`. Other orgtbl features
are not supported. In particular, to get non-default column alignment,
you'll need to add colons as above.

[PHP Markdown Extra tables]: https://michelf.ca/projects/php-markdown/extra/#table

### Extension: `table_attributes` ###

Attributes may be attached to tables by including them at the end
of the caption. (For the syntax, see
[`header_attributes`][Extension: `header_attributes`].)

      : Here's the caption. {#ident .class key="value"}

    if "String.Escape" in name or "String.Interpol" in name: return "SpecialChar"
    if "String.Regex" in name: return "SpecialString"
    if "String" in name: return "String"
    if "Number.Float" in name: return "Float"
    if "Number.Hex" in name or "Number.Oct" in name or "Number.Bin" in name: return "BaseN"
    if "Number" in name: return "DecVal"
    if name.startswith("Token.Operator.Word"): return "Keyword"
    if name.startswith("Token.Operator"): return "Operator"
    if name.startswith("Token.Error"): return "Error"
    if name.startswith("Token.Generic.Emph") or name.startswith("Token.Generic.Strong"): return None
    return None

def tokenize_code(code,lang):
    # returns lines tokens merged adjacent equal types
    low=lang.lower()
    # Simple custom for a few languages could be improved later; begin with pygments if available
    try:
        from pygments.lexers import get_lexer_by_name
        from pygments import lex
        alias=LANG_ALIASES.get(low,low)
        if alias is None: raise Exception("no lexer")
        lexer=get_lexer_by_name(alias)
        toks=[]
        for tt,txt in lex(code,lexer):
            if txt=="": continue
            toks.append((map_pygments_token(tt),txt))
    except Exception:
        toks=[(None,code)]
    # split into lines preserving no final newline semantics: code may not end with newline; lexer may add newline at end. Normalize splitting merged tokens.
    lines=[[]]
    for typ,txt in toks:
        parts=txt.split("\n")
        for idx,p in enumerate(parts):
            if idx>0: lines.append([])
            if p: lines[-1].append((typ,p))
    # If code ends with newline, pygments will create an extra empty line after final \n, but original code blocks content usually no trailing newline (reader strips). If code string ends with \n, pandoc line tokenizer might treat... We'll not preserve final empty line if the final line from splitting is empty and lexer-added \n caused it when code didn't end with \n; Python split logic only appends when token includes \n - lexers append \n automatically to text if missing. That creates an extra empty line. To detect: if not code.endswith("\n") and lines and lines[-1]==[] and len(lines)>1: pop last.
    if lines and lines[-1]==[] and not code.endswith("\n"):
        lines.pop()
    # Merge adjacent same type in each line
    merged=[]
    for line in lines:
        m=[]
        for typ,txt in line:
            if m and m[-1][0]==typ: m[-1]=(typ,m[-1][1]+txt)
            else: m.append((typ,txt))
        merged.append(m)
    return merged

def make_sections(blocks, slide_level=None, base_level=0, number_sections=False, number_offset=None):
    """Return blocks where Header hierarchy is wrapped in Div blocks with _section flag and classes section / levelN.
    If slide_level given, sections above (?) In Pandoc makeSections: headers create nested sections for all levels; slide formats writer uses slideLevel to determine slide Divs differently. For section-divs HTML, this matches.

            new_header={"t":"Header","c":[level,["",list(hattr[1]),list(hattr[2])],b["c"][2]]}
            if number:

def build_toc_tree(blocks, depth=3):
    # Return list of (header, children, number-or-None) for headers at top level / sections recursively flattened in order, filtered level <= depth and not unlisted.
    headers=[]
    def walk(bs):
        for b in bs:
            t=b.get("t")
            if t=="Header":
                if b["c"][0]<=depth and "unlisted" not in b["c"][1][1]:
                    headers.append(b)
            elif t in ("Div",):

            elif t=="BlockQuote":

    walk(blocks)

    root=[]; stack=[(0,root)]
    counters=[0]*6
    for h in headers:
        level=h["c"][0]
        counters[level-1]+=1
        for i in range(level,6): counters[i]=0
        number=".".join(str(x) for x in counters[:level] if x!=0)
        node=(h,[],number)
        while len(stack)>1 and stack[-1][0]>=level: stack.pop()
        stack[-1][1].append(node)
        stack.append((level,node[1]))
    return root

import subprocess, os, json, zipfile, io
os.chdir("/tmp")
candidates="md markdown mkd mkdn mdwn mdown markdn txt text rmd qmd lhs html htm xhtml shtml tex latex ltx ctx rst rest org json native hs xml docx odt ott epub pptx potx rtf pdf ipynb csv tsv bib bibtex djot typ typst man 1 2 3 ms adoc asciidoc asc wiki mediawiki textile muse fb2 icml opml dbk docbook tei texinfo texi s5 slidy slideous dzslides revealjs beamer context ctx csljson yaml yml lua zip chunkedhtml zimwiki zim xwiki jira dokuwiki tikiwiki twiki vimwiki creole t2t pod pm ris endnotexml bits jats haddock xlsx mdoc djvu".split()
doc=b"# Head *Em*\n\nPara **strong** [link](url)\n\n- item\n"
def run_out_ext(ext):
    path=f"/tmp/mapout.{ext}" if ext else "/tmp/mapout"
    try: os.remove(path)
    except: pass
    r=subprocess.run(['/tmp/executable','-o',path],input=doc,capture_output=True)
    data=b""
    if os.path.exists(path):
        data=open(path,'rb').read()
    return r,data
def run_explicit(fmt):
    r=subprocess.run(['/tmp/executable','-t',fmt],input=doc,capture_output=True)
    return r.stdout
formats=open("/tmp/out.txt").read().splitlines()
explicit={}
for f in formats:
    if f in ("pdf","ipynb","epub","epub2","epub3","docx","odt","pptx","chunkedhtml"): continue
    explicit[f]=run_explicit(f)
results={}
for ext in candidates:
    r,data=run_out_ext(ext)
    matches=[f for f,d in explicit.items() if d==data]
    iszip = data[:2]==b'PK'
    zim=None
    if iszip:
        try:
            z=zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)); names=z.namelist()[:6]
            if any(n.startswith('word/') for n in z.namelist()): zim='docx'
            elif any(n.startswith('ppt/') for n in z.namelist()): zim='pptx'
            elif 'mimetype' in z.namelist():
                mt=z.read('mimetype')
                zim='epub' if b'epub' in mt else 'odt'
            else: zim='zip:'+str(names)
        except Exception as e: zim=str(e)
    if ext=='ipynb' and data.startswith(b'{'): matches=['ipynb']
    results[ext]=(r.returncode,r.stderr.decode(),matches,zim,data[:80])
    print(ext,r.returncode,repr(r.stderr.decode()[:120]),matches,zim)
json.dump(results,open("/tmp/extmap_out.json","w"),default=str)

def normalize_tokens(tokens):
    toks=list(tokens)
    out=[]
    i=0
    while i < len(toks):
        tok=toks[i]
        if tok[0]=='comment':
            col=tok[2] if len(tok)>2 else 1
            if col==1:
                if i+1 < len(toks) and toks[i+1][0]=='text' and toks[i+1][1].startswith('\n'):
                    toks[i+1]=('text',toks[i+1][1][1:])
            i+=1; continue
        if tok[0]=='expr':
            # Partials consume a following newline when at end of line
            try:
                info=parse_expr(tok[1])
            except Exception:
                info={"partial":None}
            if info.get("partial") is not None:
                next_text=toks[i+1] if i+1<len(toks) else None
                at_line_end = (next_text is None) or (next_text[0]=='text' and next_text[1].startswith('\n'))
                # Determine standalone prefix from previous text tail
                prefix=None
                if at_line_end:
                    if not out:
                        prefix=""
                    elif out[-1][0]=='text':
                        tail=out[-1][1].rsplit('\n',1)[-1]
                        if tail.strip(' \t')=="": prefix=tail
                    else:
                        # previous token was on an earlier line if its line number < this token line
                        prev_line=out[-1][3] if len(out[-1])>3 and isinstance(out[-1][3],int) else None
                        if prev_line is not None and tok[2]>prev_line: prefix=" "
                    if next_text is not None and next_text[1].startswith('\n'):
                        toks[i+1]=('text',next_text[1][1:])
                if prefix is not None:
                    tok=('expr',tok[1],tok[2],tok[3],prefix)
                out.append(tok); i+=1; continue
            out.append(tok); i+=1; continue
        if tok[0]=='control':
            name=tok[1]
            next_text=toks[i+1] if i+1<len(toks) else None
            at_line_end = (next_text is None) or (next_text[0]=='text' and next_text[1].startswith('\n'))
            # Is this control at the start of a source line (ignoring whitespace)?
            at_line_start=False; prefix_tail=""
            if not out:
                at_line_start=True
            elif out[-1][0]=='text':
                tail=out[-1][1].rsplit('\n',1)[-1]
                if tail.strip(' \t')=="" and ('\n' in out[-1][1] or len(out)==1):
                    at_line_start=True; prefix_tail=tail
            else:
                prev_line=out[-1][3] if len(out[-1])>3 and isinstance(out[-1][3],int) else None
                if prev_line is not None and tok[3]>prev_line:
                    at_line_start=True
            consume=False
            if at_line_end:
                if name in ('if','for','elseif','else','sep'):
                    consume=True
                elif name in ('endif','endfor') and at_line_start:
                    consume=True
            if at_line_start and prefix_tail:
                out[-1]=('text',out[-1][1][:-len(prefix_tail)])
            if consume and next_text is not None:
                if next_text[1].startswith('\r\n'):
                    toks[i+1]=('text',next_text[1][2:])
                elif next_text[1].startswith('\n'):
                    toks[i+1]=('text',next_text[1][1:])
            out.append(tok); i+=1; continue
        out.append(tok); i+=1
    return [t for t in out if not (t[0]=='text' and t[1]=="")]

import struct, zlib, os, datetime, zipfile

def get_zip_datetime():
    epoch=os.environ.get("SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH")
    ts=None
    if epoch is not None and epoch.strip()!="":
        try: ts=int(epoch)
        except: ts=None
    if ts is None:
        dt=datetime.datetime.utcnow()
    else:

    if dt.year<1980: dt=datetime.datetime(1980,1,1,0,0,0)
    if dt.year>2107: dt=datetime.datetime(2107,12,31,23,59,58)
    return dt

def dos_datetime(dt):
    dos_time=(dt.hour<<11)|(dt.minute<<5)|(dt.second//2)
    dos_date=((dt.year-1980)<<9)|(dt.month<<5)|dt.day
    return dos_time,dos_date

def make_zip(files):
    """files: list of (name, bytes) or (name,(bytes,method)) method is zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED/Stored codes 8/0"""
    dt=get_zip_datetime(); dost, dosd=dos_datetime(dt)
    out=bytearray(); central=[]
    for item in files:
        name=item[0]; data=item[1]; method=8
        if isinstance(data,tuple):
            content=data[0]; method=data[1] if len(data)>1 else 8
        else: content=data
        if isinstance(content,str): content=content.encode()
        name_b=name.encode('utf-8')
        crc=zlib.crc32(content)&0xffffffff
        if method==8:
            comp=zlib.compressobj(6,zlib.DEFLATED,-15); cdata=comp.compress(content)+comp.flush()
        else:
            cdata=content; method=0
        offset=len(out)
        out += struct.pack('<IHHHHHIIIHH',0x04034b50,20,2050,method,dost,dosd,crc,len(cdata),len(content),len(name_b),0)
        out += name_b; out += cdata
        central.append((name_b,method,crc,len(cdata),len(content),offset))
    cd_start=len(out)
    for name_b,method,crc,cs,us,offset in central:
        out += struct.pack('<IHHHHHHIIIHHHHHII',0x02014b50,0,20,2050,method,dost,dosd,crc,cs,us,len(name_b),0,0,0,0,0,offset)
        out += name_b
    cd_size=len(out)-cd_start

    epoch=os.environ.get("SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH")
    ts=None
    if epoch is not None and epoch.strip()!="":
        try: ts=int(epoch)
        except: ts=None
    if ts is None:
        dt=datetime.datetime.utcnow()
    else:
        dt=datetime.datetime.utcfromtimestamp(ts) if ts>=0 else datetime.datetime(1980,1,1)
    if dt.year<1980: dt=datetime.datetime(1980,1,1,0,0,0)
    if dt.year>2107: dt=datetime.datetime(2107,12,31,23,59,58)
    return dt

def dos_datetime(dt):
    dos_time=(dt.hour<<11)|(dt.minute<<5)|(dt.second//2)
    dos_date=((dt.year-1980)<<9)|(dt.month<<5)|dt.day
    return dos_time,dos_date

def make_zip(files):
    """files: list of (name, bytes) or (name,(bytes,method)) method is zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED/Stored codes 8/0"""
    dt=get_zip_datetime(); dost, dosd=dos_datetime(dt)
    out=bytearray(); central=[]
    for item in files:
        name=item[0]; data=item[1]; method=8
        if isinstance(data,tuple):
            content=data[0]; method=data[1] if len(data)>1 else 8
        else: content=data
        if isinstance(content,str): content=content.encode()
        name_b=name.encode('utf-8')
        crc=zlib.crc32(content)&0xffffffff
        if method==8:
            comp=zlib.compressobj(6,zlib.DEFLATED,-15); cdata=comp.compress(content)+comp.flush()
        else:
            cdata=content; method=0
        offset=len(out)
        out += struct.pack('<IHHHHHIIIHH',0x04034b50,20,2050,method,dost,dosd,crc,len(cdata),len(content),len(name_b),0)
        out += name_b; out += cdata
        central.append((name_b,method,crc,len(cdata),len(content),offset))
    cd_start=len(out)
    for name_b,method,crc,cs,us,offset in central:
        out += struct.pack('<IHHHHHHIIIHHHHHII',0x02014b50,0,20,2050,method,dost,dosd,crc,cs,us,len(name_b),0,0,0,0,0,offset)
        out += name_b
    cd_size=len(out)-cd_start
    out += struct.pack('<IHHHHIIH',0x06054b50,0,0,len(central),len(central),cd_size,cd_start,0)
    return bytes(out)

# Multi-format markup writers - initial implementation (expanded in stages)
from ..ast import stringify
from .markdown import write_markdown

def write_markup(fmt,doc,opts,exts,app):
    # For formats not yet specialized, use plain text writer as a safe fallback (never crashes).
    # Specific writers are added in this module gradually; at this stage we delegate known close formats:
    if fmt in ("djot",):
        # Djot is close to markdown for simple docs
        return write_markdown(doc,opts,exts,"markdown")
    if fmt in ("bibtex","biblatex"):
        from .biblio import write_bibtex
        return write_bibtex(doc,opts,fmt),{}
    # Use specialized implementation registry if present
    try:
        from .markup_impl import WRITERS
        if fmt in WRITERS:
            return WRITERS[fmt](doc,opts,exts,app)
    except ImportError:
        pass
    return write_markdown(doc,opts,exts,"plain")

for i in range(start,len(lines)):
    l=lines[i]
    # strip strings crudely with tokenize? Use simple scan handling quotes
    bal=0;inq=None;esc=False
    for ch in l:
        if inq:
            if esc:esc=False
            elif ch=='\\':esc=True
            elif ch==inq:inq=None
            continue
        if ch in ('"',"'"):inq=ch;continue
        if ch=='(':bal+=1
        elif ch==')':bal-=1
    if bal<0:
        # remove -bal trailing closing parens from end (rstripped)
        stripped=l.rstrip()
        for _ in range(-bal):
            assert stripped.endswith(')');stripped=stripped[:-1]
        lines[i]=stripped;print(i,lines[i])
open(p,'w').write("\n".join(lines)+"\n")
PY

./compile.sh && for f in opendocument icml; do echo ===$f; diff -u /tmp/refout/std.$f <(./executable -f markdown -t $f /tmp/stdoc.md) | head -n 100; done"}

def esc_rtf(s):
    out=""
    fallbacks={'“':'"','”':'"','‘':"\'",'’':"\'",'–':'-','—':'-','•':'*'}
    for ch in s:
        if ch=='\':out+=r'\'
        elif ch=='{':out+=r'\{'
        elif ch=='}':out+=r'\}'
        elif ord(ch)>127:

    return out

import re
from ..ast import B

def parse_djot(text,opts,exts,app):
    # Translate Djot emphasis/strong syntax to Markdown syntax outside code spans, then use markdown parser.
    translated=translate_djot_inlines(text)
    from .markdown import parse_markdown
    # Use markdown extensions for parsing, but Djot headings should not get auto IDs in Header (Div gets it) - disable auto_identifiers in parser ext copy
    from ..formats import parse_format_spec
    _,mdexts,_,_=parse_format_spec('markdown','reader')
    mdexts=dict(mdexts)
    if not exts.get('auto_identifiers',False):
        mdexts['auto_identifiers']=False
    doc,ctx=parse_markdown(translated,opts,mdexts,"djot")
    blocks=sectionize(doc.get("blocks",[]))
    return {"meta":doc.get("meta",{}),"blocks":blocks}

def translate_djot_inlines(text):
    lines=[]
    in_fence=False
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if re.match(r'^\s*```',line):in_fence=not in_fence;lines.append(line);continue
        if in_fence:lines.append(line);continue
        # Convert _emph_ to *emph* and *strong* to **strong**, preserving code spans. Simple scanner.
        out="";i=0
        while i<len(line):
            if line[i]=='`':
                end=line.find('`',i+1)
                if end==-1:out+=line[i:];break
                out+=line[i:end+1];i=end+1;continue
            if line[i]=='_' and (i==0 or line[i-1].isspace()) :
                end=line.find('_',i+1)
                if end!=-1:out+='*'+line[i+1:end]+'*';i=end+1;continue
            if line[i]=='*' and not line.startswith('**',i) and (i==0 or line[i-1].isspace()):
                end=line.find('*',i+1)
                if end!=-1:out+='**'+line[i+1:end]+'**';i=end+1;continue
            out+=line[i];i+=1
        lines.append(out)
    return "\n".join(lines)+"\n"

def sectionize(blocks):
    # Convert heading hierarchy to nested Div sections with id based heading text (Djot spec: identifiers are heading text with spaces -> -, punctuation removed, case preserved)
    root=[];stack=[(0,root)]
    used=set()
    for b in blocks:
        if b.get("t")=="Header":
            lvl=b["c"][0]
            while len(stack)>1 and stack[-1][0]>=lvl:stack.pop()
            title_text="".join(x.get("c","") if x.get("t")=="Str" else " " if x.get("t")=="Space" else "" for x in b["c"][2]).strip()
            # Djot section ID generation: replace spaces and punctuation - simplified
            sid=re.sub(r'\s+','-',title_text).strip('-') or "section"
            # uniqueness with -2 etc in Djot spec maybe -1
            base=sid;n=1
            while sid in used:
                n+=1;sid=f"{base}-{n}"
            used.add(sid)
            heading={"t":"Header","c":[lvl,["",[],[]],b["c"][2]]}
            div=B("Div",[[sid,["section"],[]],[heading]])
            stack[-1][1].append(div);stack.append((lvl,div["c"][1]))
        else:
            stack[-1][1].append(b)
    return root
PY
